artworks.title: Silver Stater of Taras (youth on dolphin)
artworks.description: Early Tarentine stater: Taras riding the dolphin Poseidon sent to save him — the city's founder as civic badge on both faces. Berlin.

artworks.title: Silver Didrachm of Taras (dolphin and wheel)
artworks.description: Munich didrachm: the dolphin-rider with a wheel reverse — Taras as the face of Magna Graecia's richest mint.

artworks.title: Silver Stater of Taras (warrior and dolphin-rider)
artworks.description: British Museum stater: cavalry reverse with Taras still astride his dolphin — the hero-founder keeping pace with the city's horsemen.

artworks.title: Gold Stater of Taras (Taras and Poseidon)
artworks.description: Berlin gold stater: Taras before his father Poseidon — the dolphin-youth's genealogy struck in precious metal.

artworks.title: Gold Stater of Taras (infant Taras and Poseidon)
artworks.description: British Museum gold: infant Taras with Poseidon — the founder's childhood under the sea-god who will send the saving dolphin.

popCulture.title: Taranto
popCulture.description: The Italian city still bears Taras' name — Greek Taras, Roman Tarentum — the dolphin-rider on every tourist badge.

popCulture.title: Taras (mythology)
popCulture.description: Son of Poseidon who rode a dolphin to the heel of Italy and founded Taras — Magna Graecia's most minted hero.
